title: CS & Sales ask consolidation lens and sprint-fit rubric
creator: Ethan Morales
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success send individual enterprise feature asks with varying levels of detail. That creates high cognitive load for PMs and engineering to triage, duplicates work across accounts, and delays feedback to customers.

Goal: Ship a lightweight consolidation lens + sprint-fit rubric that CS/Sales can apply during intake calls (and that intake engineers can run) to produce a standardized ‘scoping packet’ for each request. The output should enable fast route decisions: quick-win (deliverable in <2 sprints), roadmap candidate (needs design/eng scoping), requires enterprise contract/legal review, or decline with rationale.

What we will deliver: a) a one-page consolidation lens checklist for PM/CS to summarize multi-account asks and detect cross-account demand; b) a 6-question sprint-fit rubric with weighted scores for impact, technical complexity, compliance/regulatory constraints, data residency, product/roadmap alignment, and urgency; c) a sample completed scoping packet template and a short runbook for frontline reps to follow; d) a dashboard query spec for intake volume and routing outcomes.

Key sections of the scoping packet:
- Request summary (one-paragraph plain language)
- Top customer(s) and use cases (list)
- Business metric requested / desired outcome (quantified if possible)
- Minimal viable acceptance criteria
- Data & compliance constraints (PII, residency, retention, logging)
- Estimated engineering touch (low/medium/high) and infra needs (Dedicated/Private)
- Suggested initial route (quick-win / roadmap / escalation / decline)
- Sales/CS ask link + supporting artifacts (email thread, recording, contract reference)

Scoring rubric (example weights):
- Impact (40%) — revenue or retention signal; cross-account lift increases score
- Effort (20%) — estimated engineering and infra cost
- Strategic alignment (15%) — fits priority pillars (e.g., Private deploys, cost controls, reliability)
- Compliance risk (15%) — data residency/KMS/legal needs (higher risk lowers score)
- Urgency (10%) — contractual deadlines or enterprise procurement timelines

Routing thresholds (example):
- Score >= 70 => Roadmap candidate (create PM epic + engineering intake)
- Score 45–69 => Scoped for quick pilot or spike (1 sprint)
- Score < 45 and no regulatory blockers => Defer / bundle into backlog
- Regulatory blocker present and high impact => Escalate to Legal & Enterprise Eng immediately

Acceptance criteria:
- Frontline reps can complete the scoping packet in under 15 minutes during a call
- PMs can make a route decision with the packet in <= 3 business days
- Dashboard shows routing distribution (quick-win / roadmap / escalation / decline) and mean time to route
- Three pilot asks processed end-to-end using the lens and rubric and feedback captured

Out-of-scope: full engineering estimates, UX mockups beyond a quick sketch, and replacing existing enterprise discovery calls.

Stakeholders: Sales leadership (Kenji Patel), CS leadership (Maria Gonzalez), Legal (Samantha Roy), Core Platform PM (me), Engineering lead (Nikhil Rao), Solutions Eng (Avery Chen).
